::: {.callout-note}
This appendix defines every term, acronym, drift finding code, and external citation used in this book. It is intended to make the bundle fully self-contained for readers who do not have access to the UIAO customer portal or the canonical ADR library. Normative authority rests with the cited Architecture Decision Records; this glossary paraphrases them for accessibility.
:::

## Part I — Glossary of Terms

**Architecture Decision Record (ADR)**
UIAO's numbered, binding governance specification. Each ADR documents a specific platform decision — its context, the options considered, the chosen approach, and the constraints that follow from it. ADRs are the authoritative source of truth for platform behavior. References in this book follow the form *ADR-NNN*. A complete list of ADRs cited in this book appears in Part III.

**Authorization Boundary**
The defined perimeter — hardware, software, data flows, and personnel — within which a federal information system operates and against which an ATO is scoped. Under FedRAMP, the authorization boundary for a Cloud Service Offering is defined in the System Security Plan. Under FedRAMP 20x, the boundary is expressed in OSCAL and referenced in the KSI stream; a boundary change is a triggering event for re-evaluation of affected KSIs.

**Authorization to Operate (ATO)**
A formal federal security authorization issued under the NIST Risk Management Framework (NIST SP 800-37) that authorizes a federal information system to operate at an accepted level of residual risk. An ATO documents the authorizing official's risk acceptance decision. Under FedRAMP, an ATO covering a Cloud Service Offering is typically preceded by a Provisional ATO (P-ATO) issued by the FedRAMP Program Management Office. See also: *Continuous Authorization to Operate (cATO)*, *Provisional ATO (P-ATO)*, *Single-ATO Reciprocity (Reciprocity)*.

**cATO (Continuous Authorization to Operate)**
The authorization model introduced by the FedRAMP 20x initiative in which a cloud service's authorization status is a live function of its Key Security Indicator stream rather than a point-in-time assessment letter. A cATO is maintained as long as all required KSIs pass; it narrows automatically to the affected organizational boundary when a KSI fails. The cATO does not eliminate the authorizing official's role — it changes that role from periodic reviewer to continuous subscriber.

**Cloud Service Offering (CSO)**
A specific, discrete cloud product or service that a Cloud Service Provider presents for FedRAMP authorization. A CSO has a defined authorization boundary, a System Security Plan, and — under FedRAMP 20x Pathway 1 — an OSCAL evidence bundle and KSI stream. A single CSP may offer multiple CSOs with separate authorization packages.

**Cloud Service Provider (CSP)**
An organization that offers cloud computing services — Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), or Software as a Service (SaaS) — to federal agencies. Under FedRAMP, CSPs are responsible for maintaining their authorization package, emitting continuous monitoring artifacts, and — under FedRAMP 20x Pathway 1 — producing machine-readable KSI assertions in OSCAL format. UIAO is deployed on and governs identity surfaces within CSP environments.

**Continuous Monitoring**
The ongoing collection, analysis, and reporting of security-relevant data for a federal information system after initial authorization. FISMA requires continuous monitoring for all federal systems. FedRAMP's traditional continuous monitoring program required monthly vulnerability scan reports, plan-of-action-and-milestones updates, and annual security reviews. FedRAMP 20x replaces this document-based cadence with automated KSI emission under Pathway 1, while preserving periodic review artifacts for Pathway 2.

**Control Baseline**
The set of NIST SP 800-53 security controls required for a federal information system at a given impact level (Low, Moderate, High). FedRAMP Moderate is the baseline most frequently required for cloud services handling federal data. FedRAMP 20x's Minimum Assessment Scope (RFC-0006) identifies the subset of Moderate Baseline controls that must be continuously evidenced via KSI under Pathway 1.

**Drift**
A deviation between the expected state of a governed identity or compliance surface (as defined by the authoritative source of record) and its observed state. In the FedRAMP context, drift arises when a KSI measurement falls below its required threshold — for example, when privileged account MFA coverage drops from 100% to 97% after new accounts are provisioned without completing enrollment. Drift is detected by the UIAO Drift Engine and expressed as structured finding objects. See also: *Drift Finding*.

**Evidence Bundle**
A structured, machine-readable compilation of security artifacts that demonstrates a cloud service's compliance posture against its authorization boundary. Under FedRAMP 20x, an evidence bundle is formatted in OSCAL and contains KSI assertions, their measurement timestamps, the systems and populations they cover, and references to the underlying data sources. UIAO's Evidence Fabric (ADR-006) assembles evidence bundles from the outputs of the identity governance scan pipeline.

**FedRAMP (Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program)**
The U.S. government's standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud products and services used by federal agencies. FedRAMP was formally authorized by the FedRAMP Authorization Act (December 2022). The program is operated by the FedRAMP Program Management Office (PMO) within GSA, in coordination with CISA, DoD, and OMB.

**FedRAMP 20x**
The modernization initiative launched by the GSA FedRAMP PMO and OMB in 2024 to accelerate and automate the FedRAMP authorization process. FedRAMP 20x introduces two authorization pathways, replaces periodic 3PAO assessment reports with continuous machine-readable KSI streams (Pathway 1), defines a Minimum Assessment Scope (RFC-0006) for continuous evidencing, and mandates OSCAL as the evidence format. The "20x" designation reflects the program's goal of reducing authorization timelines by an order of magnitude through automation.

**Ghost Credential**
A service account, API key, or workload identity credential that persists after the system or role it was created for has been decommissioned, retired, or replaced. Ghost credentials retain the access permissions assigned at creation and are not covered by any access review cycle because no active system or owner claims them. In the FedRAMP context, ghost credentials within a CSO's authorization boundary constitute an undisclosed residual access surface that may invalidate KSI assertions about privilege hygiene.

**Key Security Indicator (KSI)**
A specific, measurable security outcome continuously emitted by a Cloud Service Provider under FedRAMP 20x Pathway 1. A KSI is not a narrative of intent — it is a timestamped, machine-readable measurement of current security state for a defined population and metric. Example: "Privileged account MFA coverage: 100%, 847/847 accounts, as of 2026-06-18T14:22Z, measured by Conditional Access policy evaluation for `DOD:DISA::cloud-identity-service`." KSIs are formatted in OSCAL and emitted on a continuous schedule. The full set of required KSIs is defined in the FedRAMP 20x KSI catalog maintained by the PMO.

**OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language)**
A NIST-developed, machine-readable language for representing security control documentation, assessment plans, assessment results, and system security plans. OSCAL is the mandated evidence format for FedRAMP 20x. UIAO's Evidence Fabric (ADR-006) produces OSCAL-compatible output; KSI assertions emitted by UIAO's FedRAMP conformance adapter (ADR-043) are formatted as OSCAL assessment results and cross-referenced to the NIST SP 800-53 control catalog.

**OrgPath**
UIAO's organizational placement model. OrgPath assigns every identity object — human, device, cloud system, or service account — a position in the federal bureau hierarchy using a colon-separated namespace path. In the FedRAMP context, OrgPath is what makes KSI assertions precise rather than aggregate: a KSI assertion that is OrgPath-resolved states the measured security outcome for a specific organizational boundary, not a blended average across the entire enterprise. OrgPath notation: `AGENCY:BUREAU::SYSTEM-NAME`.

Examples:
- `DOD:DISA::cloud-identity-service` — the cloud identity service managed by DISA within DoD
- `HHS:CMS::mco-portal` — the managed care organization portal within the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

**OrgTree**
The hierarchical registry of organizational nodes that OrgPath paths are validated against. OrgTree maps agency codes and bureau names to their canonical positions in the federal hierarchy. OrgPath values that do not resolve against OrgTree are flagged as governance gaps. In the FedRAMP context, OrgTree is the reference that determines which KSI assertions belong to which agency authorization packages.

**Pathway 1 (Modernized)**
The FedRAMP 20x authorization track in which a Cloud Service Provider continuously emits KSI assertions in OSCAL format, replacing the traditional 3PAO assessment report cycle. Under Pathway 1, the authorization decision is a live function of the KSI stream. CSPs that have instrumented their environments to produce continuous, machine-readable evidence of the Minimum Assessment Scope controls qualify for Pathway 1.

**Pathway 2 (Traditional)**
The FedRAMP 20x authorization track that retains the Third Party Assessment Organization (3PAO)-led assessment model, with periodic assessment reports and continuous monitoring artifacts. Pathway 2 is the fallback for CSPs whose environments cannot yet produce the OSCAL KSI stream required by Pathway 1. UIAO supports both pathways: Pathway 1 through the KSI emission pipeline, Pathway 2 through the evidence bundle lifecycle governance in ADR-016.

**Provisional ATO (P-ATO)**
A FedRAMP authorization issued by the FedRAMP Program Management Office's Joint Authorization Board (JAB) or by a federal agency that serves as the basis for reciprocal reuse by other agencies. A P-ATO means that the CSO's security package has been reviewed and accepted by a federal entity with program-wide standing; individual agencies can issue their own ATO on the basis of the P-ATO review without repeating the full assessment. P-ATOs are the primary vehicle for the Single-ATO Reciprocity model in ADR-054.

**Reciprocity**
The principle, defined in ADR-054, that a federal information system authorized under one ATO framework (e.g., a FedRAMP P-ATO) should be recognized as authorized across participating agencies without requiring a separate full ATO for each deployment. Reciprocity reduces duplicative assessment burden and accelerates agency adoption of already-authorized cloud services. The FedRAMP Authorization Act (2022) codifies reciprocity as a statutory requirement: agencies may not require a CSP to undergo a separate assessment for a CSO that already holds a FedRAMP authorization.

**Third Party Assessment Organization (3PAO)**
An organization accredited by the American Association for Laboratory Accreditation (A2LA) and recognized by FedRAMP to perform independent security assessments of Cloud Service Offerings. Under the traditional FedRAMP model, a 3PAO conducts the annual assessment and produces the Security Assessment Report that supports the ATO. Under FedRAMP 20x Pathway 1, the continuous KSI stream replaces most of the periodic 3PAO assessment cycle, though 3PAOs retain a role in validating initial KSI implementation and in Pathway 2 assessments.

**VDR (Vulnerability Disclosure Report)**
A structured report documenting known vulnerabilities in a Cloud Service Offering, their severity, their current remediation status, and any accepted risk decisions. Under FedRAMP, VDRs are submitted as part of the continuous monitoring package. FedRAMP 20x integrates vulnerability management data as a KSI category: patch currency for critical CVEs is a continuous measurement rather than a periodic report.

## Part II — Drift Finding Codes

The following drift finding codes are used in this book. Each is a string constant in the UIAO drift taxonomy. The format is `DRIFT-CLASS::subtype`.

| Code | Severity | Posture | Trigger | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ai-ato-gap` | P2 | NEVER_AUTOFIX | Deployed or piloted federal system lacks a current ATO | Initiate or locate an ATO; link `system_name_ato` to UIAO ATO registry |
| `DRIFT-IDENTITY::ai-no-orgpath` | P2 | PER_POLICY | Organizational placement cannot be derived; bureau field absent | Confirm bureau affiliation; update source record; re-run scanner |
| `DRIFT-IDENTITY::ai-unowned` | P2 | NEVER_AUTOFIX | No named identity governance contact for the system | Assign a named bureau identity governance contact; update source record |
| `DRIFT-IDENTITY::ai-shadow` | **P1** | NEVER_AUTOFIX | System present in UIAO registry but absent from authoritative inventory | Submit system to authoritative inventory; governance-board review required |
| `DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ai-agentic-ungoverned` | **P1** | NEVER_AUTOFIX | Agentic system (L4 actor) deployed without ATO | (1) Create OrgPath record with named contact; (2) Initiate or link ATO; (3) Enroll all credentials in rotation schedule |
| `DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ai-ato-gap` (FedRAMP KSI failure) | P2 | NEVER_AUTOFIX | One or more KSIs in the FedRAMP 20x stream report a failing measurement | Remediate the failing KSI condition; re-emit KSI assertion after remediation; notify authorizing official |
| `DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ato-reciprocity-gap` | P2 | PER_POLICY | CSO holds a P-ATO but consuming agency has not yet issued its own ATO on that basis | Agency issues reciprocal ATO citing the P-ATO package; UIAO ATO registry is updated to reflect agency-level recognition |

**Gate behavior:** P1 findings halt the governance gate — no new identity provisioning, access expansion, or OrgPath assignments proceed through the automated pipeline in the affected bureau until the finding is resolved or a written risk acceptance is filed by an authorizing official. P2 findings are routed to the responsible governance contact for disposition within the configured SLA window.

**KSI failure posture:** A failing KSI does not automatically revoke an existing cATO, but it narrows the authorization scope to exclude the organizational boundary for which the KSI failed and triggers a P2 finding routed to the authorizing official. Continued failure beyond the configured remediation window escalates to P1.

## Part III — Architecture Decision Records Cited in This Book

Architecture Decision Records are UIAO's binding governance specifications. The records below are cited in this book. Authoritative text is available through the UIAO customer portal at `/docs/adr/`.

**ADR-006 — Evidence Fabric**
Defines UIAO's evidence collection, storage, and OSCAL correlation architecture. The Evidence Fabric receives structured finding objects from the Drift Engine and produces compliance evidence bundles for auditor and authorizing official consumption. In the FedRAMP 20x context, the Evidence Fabric assembles the OSCAL-formatted KSI assertions and evidence references that constitute the cATO data feed.

**ADR-016 — Evidence Bundle Lifecycle**
Governs the sealing and retention of evidence records. Sealed evidence bundles are immutable audit artifacts. For FedRAMP, the evidence bundle produced at each KSI evaluation cycle is a sealed artifact retained for the duration of the ATO plus the applicable statutory retention period. ADR-016 specifies a 7-year retention minimum for compliance attestation records. Pathway 2 periodic assessment artifacts are governed under this ADR.

**ADR-040 — Drift Engine**
Defines the six-phase drift orchestration pipeline: collect, normalize, compare, classify, gate, and remediate. The FedRAMP conformance adapter (ADR-043) operates as a collect and classify module within this pipeline. ADR-040 defines the gate function: any P1 finding produces a HALT decision; P2 findings are routed for operator disposition.

**ADR-043 — FedRAMP Conformance Adapter**
The governing ADR for UIAO's FedRAMP integration. Defines the adapter architecture that maps UIAO's identity governance outputs — OrgPath-resolved identity measurements, drift findings, and evidence records — to the FedRAMP 20x KSI format and OSCAL schema. ADR-043 specifies the KSI catalog mapping, the evidence bundle assembly process, and the Pathway 1 vs. Pathway 2 routing logic.

**ADR-054 — Single-ATO Reciprocity**
Defines how UIAO recognizes ATOs issued under different federal frameworks (FedRAMP P-ATO, DISA, agency-specific) without requiring re-authorization for every deployment. ADR-054 governs the cross-walk between the FedRAMP authorization registry and agency-level ATO records, produces `DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ato-reciprocity-gap` findings when the cross-walk fails, and defines the evidence records that support reciprocal recognition.

**ADR-092 — Active Governance**
Defines UIAO's core operating posture as a reconciliation control plane, the control-plane/data-plane boundary, the provider-incorporation contract, and the L0–L4 actuation ladder. In the FedRAMP context, the UIAO identity governance pipeline operates at L1 (observe and alert) by default, with promotion to L3 (gated actuation — automated remediation within policy scope) available for KSI-failing conditions after a governance-board decision.

**ADR-106 — FedRAMP 20x**
The governing ADR for this book's central subject. Defines UIAO's alignment to the FedRAMP 20x initiative, the Pathway 1 and Pathway 2 adapter architectures, the KSI catalog mapping to UIAO drift finding codes, the OSCAL evidence bundle format, and the cATO status model. ADR-106 establishes how OrgPath-resolved identity measurements become the KSI assertions that authorizing officials subscribe to.

## Part IV — UIAO Specifications Cited

**UIAO_132 — FedRAMP Conformance Specification**
Defines the operational schema, KSI field mappings, and scanner interface for UIAO's FedRAMP conformance adapter (ADR-043). UIAO_132 specifies: the 18 KSI types in the FedRAMP 20x catalog and their mapping to UIAO drift finding codes; the OSCAL serialization format for KSI assertions; the OrgPath resolution algorithm for KSI scope attribution; and the evidence bundle assembly sequence. UIAO_132 is the operational specification that ADR-043 and ADR-106 leave implicit.

---

## Part V — Federal Mandates Referenced

**FedRAMP Authorization Act (2022)** — Division U, Title II, Subtitle B of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Pub. L. 117-263, December 23, 2022). Codifies FedRAMP as a statutory program, establishes the FedRAMP Board, requires agencies to use FedRAMP-authorized cloud services whenever practicable, and mandates reciprocal recognition of existing FedRAMP authorizations. The Act establishes that agencies may not require a separate, full security assessment of a CSO that already holds a FedRAMP authorization unless the agency has specific, documented reasons for doing so.

**FISMA 2014 — Federal Information Security Modernization Act** — Pub. L. 113-283 (December 18, 2014). Requires federal agencies to develop, document, and implement agency-wide information security programs for all federal information systems. FISMA establishes the annual reporting requirement, continuous monitoring obligation, and risk-based ATO framework that FedRAMP and UIAO operate within. The FISMA categorization (Low, Moderate, High) drives the control baseline against which KSIs are evaluated.

**OMB Circular A-130 — Managing Information as a Strategic Resource** (July 28, 2016). OMB's overarching policy framework for federal information resources management. Appendix I establishes responsibilities for protecting federal information resources, including the requirement that agencies implement risk management programs consistent with NIST guidelines. A-130 is the policy foundation on which FISMA's operational requirements rest.

**OMB M-23-10 — The Registration and Use of .gov Domains by the Federal Government** (February 2023). While primarily addressing .gov domain registration, M-23-10 includes provisions relevant to FedRAMP-authorized services used to host federal digital services, including identity and access management surfaces. Referenced for its authorization boundary implications for agency cloud deployments.

**FedRAMP 20x Initiative Documentation** — GSA/OMB initiative documentation including: RFC-0006 (Minimum Assessment Scope specification defining the KSI catalog), the FedRAMP 20x Pathway 1 and Pathway 2 framework documents, and the OSCAL KSI schema specification. Published and maintained by the FedRAMP PMO at [fedramp.gov/20x](https://www.fedramp.gov/20x) and the FedRAMP automation GitHub repository (github.com/GSA/fedramp-automation).

## Part VI — NIST Controls Referenced

The following NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls are mapped to FedRAMP 20x KSI categories and UIAO drift findings in this book:

| Control | Title | FedRAMP 20x / UIAO Relevance |
|---|---|---|
| **CA-2** | Control Assessments | 3PAO assessment report (Pathway 2) and KSI-based continuous assessment (Pathway 1) are both CA-2 artifacts |
| **CA-5** | Plan of Action and Milestones | POA&M entries for failing KSIs are the CA-5 artifact under FedRAMP 20x; UIAO routes P2 drift findings to the POA&M tracking surface |
| **CA-7** | Ongoing Assessments | The FedRAMP KSI stream is the CA-7 continuous monitoring record under Pathway 1; evidence bundle sealing cadence maps to CA-7 frequency requirements |
| **CM-6** | Configuration Settings | KSIs for configuration hardening (e.g., encryption-at-rest, TLS version, key rotation cadence) are CM-6 evidence records |
| **CM-8** | System Component Inventory | OrgPath-resolved identity records for cloud systems are CM-8 component inventory entries; KSI assertions reference the CM-8 inventory for scope attribution |
| **RA-5** | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | VDR and patch-currency KSIs are RA-5 evidence; critical CVE remediation SLA compliance is a Pathway 1 KSI category |
| **SA-9** | External System Services | FedRAMP authorization of a CSO is the SA-9 authorization record for agency deployments; reciprocity (ADR-054) is the SA-9 governance mechanism |
| **SI-2** | Flaw Remediation | Patch currency and critical vulnerability remediation KSIs are SI-2 continuous evidence; KSI failure on SI-2 controls triggers a P2 finding |

## Part VII — External Standards and Publications

**NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 — Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and Organizations**. The RMF process under which federal ATOs are issued. FedRAMP is an implementation of the RMF tailored for cloud services. The cATO model introduced by FedRAMP 20x extends the RMF Step 6 (Monitor) by replacing periodic reporting artifacts with continuous KSI evidence, but operates within the same fundamental authorization structure.

**OSCAL Specification (NIST)**. The Open Security Controls Assessment Language, developed by NIST and published at [pages.nist.gov/OSCAL](https://pages.nist.gov/OSCAL). OSCAL defines machine-readable formats for system security plans, assessment plans, assessment results, and plans of action and milestones. FedRAMP 20x mandates OSCAL for all Pathway 1 evidence bundles. UIAO's Evidence Fabric (ADR-006) produces OSCAL assessment result documents that serve as the KSI submission artifact.

**FedRAMP Automation GitHub Repository** (github.com/GSA/fedramp-automation). GSA's public repository for FedRAMP OSCAL schemas, validation tools, and Pathway 1 implementation guidance. The repository includes: the FedRAMP OSCAL profile (mapping FedRAMP control baselines), the KSI schema definition, sample evidence bundles, and RFC-0006 (Minimum Assessment Scope). The authoritative reference for implementing UIAO's ADR-043 FedRAMP conformance adapter in a production environment.

**NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 — Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations**. The control catalog from which the NIST control mappings in Part VI are drawn and against which FedRAMP control baselines are defined. The Moderate Baseline from SP 800-53 Rev 5 is the control set most frequently applicable to federal cloud deployments governed under FedRAMP.
